approach.method_basis: ChemTS runs Monte Carlo tree search over the prefixes of a SMILES string. Each node in the tree is a partial molecule, and the search picks which prefix to extend using an upper confidence bound that balances how well that branch has scored against how rarely it has been tried. A frozen language model completes the chosen prefix into a whole molecule by stochastic rollout, and the score that comes back is propagated up the path that produced it, so the tree accumulates a value estimate for every prefix.
approach.novelty: This root commits to keeping the rollout prior completely frozen and putting all task adaptation into the tree statistics, so nothing about the generative model changes during an objective. It initializes each fresh tree's statistics from the supplied initial observations rather than from an empty tree, and uses an explicit exploration constant of one half against the completed visit counts, which is the specific balance the method statement leaves open.

observed_bottleneck: There is no parent or campaign evidence yet. The benchmark supplies scarce task-local scores, so unguided full-sequence sampling can expend feedback on unrelated molecular families. This root tests whether sharing observed rewards across SMILES prefixes guides a frozen generative model toward promising families within the frozen evaluation budget. A usable corpus-trained rollout prior is an unverified prerequisite.
hypothesis: Search an expanding SMILES prefix tree with UCT using task-local observed returns, expand prefixes from a frozen corpus-trained autoregressive RNN, complete molecules by stochastic RNN rollouts, and backpropagate accepted oracle scores through their generating paths.

finding_summary.headline: Frozen-prior tree search reproduced across three seeds; strong docking scores and concentrated batches persisted
finding_summary.insights:
The search behavior and strong docking outcomes now recur across independently prepared priors, so the original result was not confined to one trained checkpoint or rollout seed. This replication does not isolate a score benefit from UCT over unguided sampling: all runs use both the corpus prior and tree adaptation, and preparation randomness changes along with search randomness. The substantial sitagliptin spread also shows that similar mechanism activation can yield materially different best molecules.

The search remains shallow at this budget. New rollout-start prefixes averaged about 3.38 tokens while completed strings averaged 38.53, and almost half the batches used a single prefix. Yet the molecular assessment finds broad ring and functional-group diversity, so concentrated short SMILES prefixes do not by themselves demonstrate chemical collapse. They may group molecules with weakly related returns. These observations make pending-rollout accounting and more chemically meaningful reward sharing plausible questions to test, without establishing that either improves final scores. Unspecified stereochemistry, size extremes and occasional awkward functional groups also persist despite the generally recognizable medicinal chemistry.
finding_summary.results:
Both added replicas confirmed the intended search mechanism. Prior weights stayed fixed throughout each task, all 2,900 accepted generated scores updated their recorded tree paths, and all 19,580 traversal choices matched the declared UCT rule. Later accepted scores entered 11,960 chosen value estimates; in 2,120 selections the empirical-mean term made the chosen branch outrank a branch with a larger exploration bonus. The new replicas added 590 prefix nodes across ten task trees and completed every ten-molecule batch without an invalid or duplicate submission.

The two new macro final Top-1 scores were 0.508151 and 0.481129, alongside the original 0.479189. The three-seed mean is 0.489490 with population standard deviation 0.013219. Task means are 0.433514 for zaleplon, 0.612739 for decoration hopping, 0.964212 for docking, 0.177507 for median_2 and 0.259477 for sitagliptin. Docking remained between 0.938221 and 0.977922 across the three seeds; sitagliptin varied more, from 0.206406 to 0.334869. Prefix concentration persisted: 141 of the 290 new batches emitted all ten molecules from one prefix, versus 76 of 145 originally.

molecular.headline: Broad aromatic scaffolds and accessible amines, with unassigned stereochemistry and a tail of oversized or chemically awkward structures
molecular.overall_character: This assessment covers the supplied seed-1 and seed-2 trajectories. The comparison baseline is seed 0 of the same Algorithm Node, not a different parent implementation. All five tasks have trajectories, each with 600 evaluated records including 580 optimizer proposals. The output spans linked and fused azaarenes, indoles, sulfur heterocycles, saturated nitrogen rings, cyclic carbonyl compounds, sulfonamides, ethers and occasional peptide-like or nucleotide-like structures. Structural variety is broad; the chemistry has not collapsed to one ring family. The digest reports ring-closure indicators in 98.79–99.66% of proposals and aromatic-atom indicators in 96.72–97.93%. These are fractions of SMILES containing those features, not aromatic atom fractions or measurements of molecular shape. Mean SMILES lengths are 38.1–40.2 characters, but the full trajectories also contain much larger structures. Conventional medicinal-chemistry frameworks predominate, supporting plausible apparent makeability, while highly extended structures and reactive or unusual functional groups make overall drug-likeness moderate. Makeability, stability and biological selectivity have not been experimentally established. Explicit stereocentre markers are absent from every proposal set, even though several high-scoring saturated-ring structures have stereogenic carbons. This is missing stereochemical specification, not absence of saturated or three-dimensional ring systems. Formal-charge counters likewise do not measure how many neutral SMILES contain protonatable amines. The recurring gaps concern chemical specification, size and polarity balance, and the arrangement of functional groups, rather than an inability to generate rings or aromatic heteroatoms.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring output consists of medium-sized phenyl/azaaryl assemblies: an N-ethyl triazole with a cyanophenyl group and a carboxybenzyl thioether, a methylsulfone-substituted linked heteroaromatic system, a chroman carboxylic acid attached to an aminopyrimidine, and morpholine-substituted fused azaarenes. Indole, benzimidazolone, ether, amide and hydroxamic-acid chemistry also appears. These are mostly recognizable, apparently makeable small-molecule frameworks. The proposal set has mean SMILES length 39.6, ring-closure rate 0.9966 and aromatic-atom rate 0.9759; its extremes include very large peptide-like, phosphorous-containing and multiply fused structures.
liabilities: The best molecule contains a thioether, and another high-scoring example contains a hydroxamic acid; these introduce oxidation-state or metal-binding questions that the supplied score does not resolve.

The final sulfur-rich example combines a thioester with an unusual hydrogen-bearing, multiply bonded sulfur linkage. Its chemical form and synthetic route are less straightforward than the conventional heteroaryl examples.
Long peptide-like chains and heavily decorated phosphorous-containing structures introduce large size, flexibility or dense polar functionality without retaining favorable scores.
missing_features: Consistent retention of the moderate size and aromatic/polar balance present in the high-scoring structures; both oversized extensions and underdecorated saturated frameworks remain in the evaluated output.
Stereochemical specification at the substituted chroman carbon is absent. The trajectories do not establish whether resolving that configuration would change this objective.

A uniquely missing target motif cannot be identified from these chemically different high scorers; their scores support more precise control of attachment patterns, not a claim that an entire ring or functional-group class is absent.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The triazole/carboxybenzyl thioether scores 0.4588223100704468 and the linked heteroaryl methylsulfone scores 0.4467986735542579. Their distinct polar groups show that no single terminal group explains the high end. The initial indole carboxamide already scores 0.3051048083696145. The seed-0 baseline best was a compact aryl/pyridyl thiourea at 0.3949199041196016; the new higher-scoring structures retain an aromatic, moderately sized character while changing the central connectivity. At the low end, both a very large peptide-like chain and the small fully saturated bridged aminoalcohol score 0.0. Thus the observed preference is for a bounded combination of size, aromatic connectivity and polar functionality, rather than simply smaller molecules or more rings. The reported median is 0.011662. A high-scoring proposal at evaluation 297 is followed by a large final phosphoramidate at 1.274785543572214e-22; the last proposals are not a uniformly favorable chemical family.

per_task.generated_character: The high end is rich in linked nitrogen heteroarenes and fused azaarenes, with amino or ether connections, thiophene/thiadiazole rings, and occasional morpholine. The best structure combines an acrylamide, methylthio-substituted pyrimidine, pyridyl ether and benzothiadiazole. Other high-scoring molecules use an aminoethylamino connection to a quinazoline-like core, or hydrazones and sulfonamides. The mean SMILES length is 39.5, ring-closure rate 0.9931 and aromatic-atom rate 0.9759. These generally resemble accessible heteroaromatic screening compounds, although some highly conjugated and extensively linked structures are chemically more demanding.
liabilities: The best molecule carries an electrophilic acrylamide and a thioether. A favorable score does not establish that either reactivity or oxidative stability is acceptable.
Hydrazones and imines among the higher-scoring and late structures leave questions of hydrolytic stability, tautomerism and double-bond geometry.
Some extensively linked aromatic structures provide substantial conjugated surface and limited saturated character; their solubility and conformational behavior are not given.
missing_features: The generator does not consistently preserve the connected azaaryl and amino/ether architecture visible at the high end when varying substituents and ring systems.

More controlled alternatives to the carbon-bonded sulfone arrangements seen at the low end are missing as an interpretable local series. The favorable sulfonamide example prevents a blanket claim that oxidized sulfur should be removed.
No particular missing target decoration or required geometry can be established from these unpaired examples alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The acrylamide-containing heteroaryl assembly scores 0.6206976589959546, and the aminoethylamino-linked azaarenes score 0.6115153965366216. The seed-0 best at 0.6060034997980885 was also an amino-linked fused azaarene, bearing a benzoic acid and a fused cyclic ketone. The recurring high-end feature is a connected, nitrogen-rich aromatic architecture with appropriately placed linkers. All six digest worst examples contain carbon-bonded sulfone linkages, including the brominated acrylamide/methylsulfone at 0.2579134792930625 and the methylsulfone indole at 0.2629377264102122. A sulfonamide-containing hydrazone scores 0.5803755601394125, so sulfur oxidation alone is not a sufficient explanation. The initial small alkyl bromide scores 0.5, the median is 0.530123, and the final sulfonylguanidine scores 0.5069001207521131. Those observations also show that a middling score is not evidence of elaborate or desirable chemistry. These are unmatched molecular contrasts, not isolated substituent effects.

per_task.generated_character: The high-scoring structures are medium-sized aromatic compounds with exposed aliphatic amines: arylpiperazines, substituted piperidines and an indanyl secondary amine connected to a fused sulfur/nitrogen heteroarene. Indanone, benzothiazole, indole-like fused systems and flexible alkyl or benzyl spacers provide varied aromatic surroundings. The proposal set remains predominantly ring-containing and aromatic, with rates 0.9966 and 0.9793 and mean SMILES length 38.1. These amine/aryl frameworks are generally synthetically recognizable, but the full output also includes neutral carbonyl-rich heterocycles and heavily halogenated phenols.
liabilities: The high-scoring chlorinated arylpiperazine includes a benzylic chloride, an electrophilic handle that warrants separate chemical assessment despite its score of 0.9375158755153281.

Several late structures accumulate bromine or iodine on phenolic aromatic systems, and one carries an azo linkage; these add substantial halogenation or chemically consequential functionality without approaching the favorable amine-containing examples.
missing_features: Consistent coverage of the exposed aliphatic amine plus aromatic-spacer arrangement is missing from much of the proposal distribution, although the generator clearly can produce it.

Controlled variation of the distance and attachment geometry between the amine and aromatic surfaces is needed to distinguish useful arrangements from the low-scoring basic imidazoline and aminoalcohol examples; basic nitrogen alone is not a sufficient observed feature.
The indanyl secondary amine and more complicated saturated polycycles have unspecified stereochemistry. No stereoisomer comparison is available.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The bromophenyl piperazine joined through a benzyl group to an indanone scores 0.9764936974373054. The indanyl secondary amine scores 0.9382214313583629, and the phenylpropyl-substituted benzothiazolyl piperidine scores 0.9351873161919285. The seed-0 best at 0.9779218035868983 used an indole-linked piperidine and a lactam, retaining an exposed aliphatic amine in a different surrounding scaffold. At the low end, the pyrrolidine nitrogen in a urea-containing sulfonamide is carbonyl-bound and scores 3.086197932883512e-05; an N-acyl piperidine scores 3.408357355512484e-05. These support a distinction between an available basic amine and simply containing nitrogen or a nitrogen ring. Availability is not sufficient: the late imidazoline-substituted phenol scores 0.008098003998695502, and an aromatic aminoalcohol scores 0.06735006158434823. The median is 0.005833, and a final halogenated naphthol scores 0.008710857097960593, showing that much of the evaluated chemistry lacks the favorable combination of basicity, spacing and aromatic environment.

per_task.generated_character: The high-scoring output combines aromatic heterocycles with cyclic carbonyl or sulfonamide chemistry: a benzofused nitrogen-containing dione bearing an N-sulfonyl azepane, a cyanoimidazole linked through an acylpiperazine to benzodioxole, sulfonylpiperazines, xanthine-like polycarbonyl rings and morpholine-containing structures. This is broader than a single fused-ring series. Mean SMILES length is 40.2, with ring-closure rate 0.9879 and aromatic-atom rate 0.9672. Most examples are conventional small-molecule combinations with plausible synthetic building blocks; the low end also contains acyclic sulfur-rich fragments, amino-acid-like structures and long flexible chains.
liabilities: The higher-scoring hydrazone example introduces an unspecified C=N geometry and a hydrolytic-stability question.

The low-scoring long-chain guanidino/phosphonic-acid structure combines a long flexible hydrophobic segment with strongly polar termini, a very different size and polarity distribution from the favorable compact ring systems.

Carbonyl- or sulfonyl-bound piperazine nitrogens should not be assumed to provide the basicity of unsubstituted aliphatic amines; those groups occur among favorable molecules here, so attenuated basicity is not itself evidence of failure.
missing_features: The output does not show a consistently favorable, precisely arranged combination of aromatic rings, cyclic carbonyl or sulfonyl groups and saturated heterocycles; those ingredients are already present separately and in varied combinations.

No specific missing reference-like scaffold or attachment pattern can be inferred from these scores alone. The evidence supports studying related arrangements of existing functional groups rather than asserting that a ring family is unavailable.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The benzofused dione/N-sulfonyl azepane scores 0.1814990197188793 and the acylpiperazine/cyanoimidazole scores 0.17716466781757798. The initial polycarbonyl fused heteroarene already scores 0.1678386594791329. The seed-0 best, an oxazolidinone-linked fused lactam/phenol assembly, scored 0.17994167047030216. The new and baseline high ends therefore contain different scaffolds with overlapping aromatic and cyclic polar features, without a large separation from ordinary starting chemistry. At the low end, a small acyclic N-hydroxythiourea scores 0.0, a long guanidino/phosphonic-acid chain scores 0.015193428136569091, and sulfamide scores 0.02668612498071339. Aromatic ring architecture combined with carbonyl/sulfonyl and saturated-ring functionality separates these examples more clearly than heteroatom abundance alone. However, the reported median of 0.109136 and the broad range of high-end scaffolds do not reveal a unique missing substructure.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring molecules are compact to medium-sized, phenyl-bearing nitrogen heterocycles with carbonyl, hydroxy or amino functionality. They include a fluorinated fused N-heterocycle with an aminotetrahydrofuran substituent, a triazolone/thioacetamide, a benzyl-substituted polycarbonyl fused heterocycle, and a hydroxyquinolone carboxamide. Other proposals include piperidines, piperazines, amidines and guanidines. Mean SMILES length is 40.1, ring-closure rate 0.9948 and aromatic-atom rate 0.9724. The ordinary heteroaromatic examples are apparently makeable, while large peptide-like chains and nucleotide polyphosphates occupy a very different part of the output.
liabilities: The best aminotetrahydrofuran structure has an N,O-acetal-like attachment and a hydroxy/carbonyl-rich heterocycle, raising chemical-form and stability questions that a SMILES score does not settle.

The high-scoring triazolone/thioacetamide contains a thioether, while late amidines introduce protonation and tautomer questions; these are properties to characterize rather than evidence of measured toxicity.
Large peptide-like and polyphosphate structures combine many polar groups and flexible connections and fall far outside the compact structures associated with the favorable scores.
missing_features: Consistent control of compact size together with the placement and number of polar groups is missing; the output repeatedly reaches both highly extended aromatic structures and peptide/polyphosphate extremes.

The tetrahydrofuran attachment carbon in the best molecule is stereogenic but unspecified. The absence of explicit stereochemistry is observable, whereas an objective benefit from resolving it has not been tested.

A particular missing fluorinated fragment, amine class or target-like connection is not established by the shown scores. Both fluorinated and unhalogenated compounds, and different nitrogen functional states, occur among the favorable examples.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluorinated fused heterocycle with hydroxy, carbonyl and aminotetrahydrofuran groups scores 0.3348688435749572. An unhalogenated triazolone/thioacetamide scores 0.25193522359670406, and the fluorobenzyl polycarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.2444857272022064. Thus neither fluorine nor an exposed basic amine is a uniquely supported requirement. The seed-0 best was a tertiary benzylamine bearing azoles at 0.23715698113688108; the seed-2 best is a hydroxyquinolone carboxamide at 0.20640632511413345. These differing favorable chemotypes suggest a restrictive combination of size and polar/aromatic features rather than a single observed motif. The large peptide-like structure and polyphosphate nucleotide score 0.0, while a very extended largely aromatic structure scores 8.786833153590336e-69. Both excessive polar complexity and excessive aromatic extension occur at the low end. Conversely, the small fluorochlorobenzamidine at the end scores only 8.674707650435866e-06, so compactness, halogenation and a basic group are not enough. The digest reports median 0.0, including many extremely small positive scores in the full trajectories.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0 over 580 optimizer proposals. Digest examples include a substituted chroman carboxylic acid, an indanyl secondary amine and an aminotetrahydrofuran-containing high scorer, each with a stereogenic carbon left unspecified. Saturated and fused ring systems are present, so the gap is specification of their configuration.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereogenic saturated structures are emitted without explicit stereochemical specification.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide the ability to specify and preserve stereochemistry at eligible centers and to compare those chemical identities using current task-local observations. These trajectories do not establish whether the absence originates in vocabulary, preprocessing or sampling, and they do not prove that the observed objectives distinguish stereoisomers.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Mean proposal SMILES lengths stay between 38.1 and 40.2, but task maxima range from 93 to 123 characters. The digest includes zero-scoring extended peptide-like and polyphosphate structures and extremely low-scoring large aromatic assemblies alongside compact high-scoring heterocycles. A small saturated bridged aminoalcohol also scores zero, so reducing size indiscriminately is not supported.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently control size and polarity while retaining an otherwise useful aromatic scaffold.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable controlled changes to scaffold extension, linker length and the number of appended polar groups around observed favorable molecules. Let local feedback determine the useful size and polarity range; a universal preference for the smallest or least polar molecules would contradict the output.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A benzyl/arylpiperazine scores 0.9764936974373054, whereas a urea-bound pyrrolidine scores 3.086197932883512e-05 and a basic imidazoline-containing aromatic compound scores 0.008098003998695502. Elsewhere, N-acyl and N-sulfonyl cyclic amines occur among the digest high scorers. The generator already supplies these functional states, but the examples do not form controlled comparisons of basicity and spacing.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks systematic local variation of amine availability and its geometric relation to neighboring aromatic groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support related molecular variants that change amine acylation or sulfonylation, spacer length or attachment position while preserving the surrounding core. Use task-local scores to learn which functional relationship is useful; neither universal amine addition nor universal removal of carbonyl/sulfonyl groups is justified.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest high scorers include an acrylamide/thioether structure at 0.6206976589959546 and a benzylic-chloride-containing arylpiperazine at 0.9375158755153281. A late proposal contains an unusual hydrogen-bearing, multiply bonded sulfur linkage and scores 5.7691712191843035e-08. Hydrazones, imines and complex phosphorous-containing structures also occur. These are observed reactivity or chemical-form questions, not measured toxicity outcomes.
transferable_gaps.gap: Favorable scaffold chemistry is not consistently accompanied by tractable, chemically well-specified functional groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make conservative functional-group and linkage alternatives available within related scaffold families, and retain explicit chemical-form information where meaningful. Evaluate alternatives using local observations and separate chemical tractability from the numerical objective; do not assume every electrophile, sulfur group or ionizable center requires exclusion.

method_name: ChemTS: UCT-guided SMILES prefix search with a frozen rollout prior
method_thesis: Anchor the root in [ChemTS](https://arxiv.org/html/1710.00616v1): train a compact autoregressive SMILES model solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus during preparation, then freeze it. For each independent objective, maintain a fresh prefix tree whose nodes hold visit counts and observed returns. Initialize its statistics from the supplied observations. Select prefixes through upper-confidence tree search, expand them using the frozen model's next-token distribution, and generate complete molecules by stochastic continuation. Backpropagate accepted oracle scores through the corresponding paths after feedback. Generate further continuations until the evaluator-announced batch contains distinct canonical structures. This is an expanding generative tree, with no corpus ranking or fixed molecular candidate set. The hypothesis is that sharing each scarce reward across its visited prefixes directs subsequent continuations toward promising molecular families quickly enough to improve the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. The root adapts tree statistics; it does not update neural parameters with rewards. The paper supports this search mechanism, but its larger, time-limited experiments do not establish performance under this benchmark's scarce feedback. Learning a useful rollout prior within permitted preparation remains an empirical prerequisite.
